cells.tense: Something is being made here right now and you are mid-motion in it.
cells.ask: Name what isn't finished yet in front of the person you're making it with, while it's still soft.
cells.core:
You can say a thing isn't done yet and stay in the room with someone while it stays undone. You don't rush to close it and you don't hold it back behind glass either — you're right there, moving with it. Going well, this looks like a conversation where the shape keeps changing and nobody panics.

You feel with the person while the edges are still soft, and that's why it holds. It is not that you know the outcome. You know how to be in the middle of something with another person and stay kind. That's what it costs: no easy certainty, and no credit for the quiet way you carry it — the mood stays open, the ground stays shared, and you keep both.
cells.sheetLine: You can sit with unfinished things and stay by someone's side.

cells.tense: You are rehearsing what's coming before it has actually arrived to meet you.
cells.ask: Pick one scene you keep playing out and drop it before you walk in.
cells.core:
You feel with people so far ahead that you start living in a version that hasn't happened yet. The dream gets more detail than the day in front of you, and the person across from you is being answered in your head before they've spoken. When this is working, you bring that same imagination to what's actually here, and it lands.

In excess, the picture crowds the room. You're not lying to anyone on purpose — you're caring ahead of time. But the rehearsing has a cost: the real hour gets compared to a scene and the scene keeps winning. Letting one scene go makes room for the one that's happening, and for the person who is standing in it waiting to be seen.

cells.tense: You stopped at a threshold longer ago than you may realize and haven't moved past it.
cells.ask: Write one line about something you felt today, and don't edit it afterward.
cells.core:
You used to trust a hunch, an image, a sense of what was true before you could show why. That has gone quiet. You learned to wave it off — be practical, call it nothing, wait for a fact. When it's working, that quick knowing is back and it's usually right; you feel it before you can argue it, and people trust you because you trust it.

The pull is thin now and connection happens through a window. You're in the room; the thing that used to arrive on its own isn't arranging itself. Start with the body, not the mind: one line, no polish. It opens the door you're standing at, even if the room beyond isn't clear yet.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped trusting what you feel before you can prove it.

cells.tense: You are moving yourself and the room in ways you would not call yours.
cells.ask: Keep one small thing lit for ten minutes a day and say, out loud, that you kept it.
cells.core:
You're already moving toward a shape that hasn't shown its face, and doing it near other people. Going well, that guesswork stays loose — it doesn't grab. But when you talk about it, you hand the credit away. A thought arrives and it's the day's mood. The room shifts and it's the room. None of it is called yours.

Somewhere in that, what you do with the not-knowing drops out of sight, and the guesses keep steering things anyway. A small repeated thing you keep for yourself puts the credit back where it belongs. The vision doesn't vanish when you claim it. It waits. It costs you the ease of being surprised by your own life.
cells.sheetLine: What you do is yours. You keep talking as if it isn't.
